correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs completely. At any Fourier zero four unit complex summands have zero sum; the monic polynomial with those roots has vanishing odd elementary coefficients, hence is even and the roots split into two antipodal pairs. A fixed matching cannot recur at two distinct frequencies because every nonzero support difference is invertible modulo the prime. Three zeros would require all three matchings and force minus one to be a p-th root of unity, impossible for odd p. Two distinct zeros force the additive relation \(x_1+x_4=x_2+x_3\). Conversely that relation gives an explicit two-zero phase choice. The all-one vector has no zero, and the one-parameter pairwise-antipodal phase family realizes exactly one zero after avoiding finitely many forbidden phases. Thus the stated attainable sets hold for every prime \(p\ge5\); finite verification is corroborative only.
